title: Number of solutions of sin n theta = 1/2 in a full turn
source: Theory P1-5.6 Quick check 1; 2n solutions of sin(n theta)=1/2 for 0 to 360 degrees
stem: How many solutions of \(\sin({n|int}\theta)=\dfrac{1}{2}\) are there for \(0^\circ\le\theta\le 360^\circ\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The equation \(\sin\phi=\dfrac{1}{2}\) has two solutions in each interval of \(360^\circ\). Here \(\phi={n|int}\theta\) runs through \({n|int}\) such intervals, so there are \({A|int}\) solutions.
steps.note: Two solutions of sin phi = 1/2 in each 360 degrees.

contexts.note: Includes the original sin 2 theta, four solutions

title: Number of solutions of cos theta = 1/2 in n full turns
source: Theory P1-5.6 Quick check 2; 2n solutions of cos theta = 1/2 for 0 to 360 n degrees
stem: How many solutions of \(\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}\) are there for \(0^\circ\le\theta\le {n|int}\times 360^\circ\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: \(\cos\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}\) has two solutions in each interval of \(360^\circ\), and the given interval is \({n|int}\) such intervals, so there are \({A|int}\) solutions.
steps.note: Two solutions in each full turn.

contexts.note: Includes the original 720 degrees, four solutions

title: Number of solutions of tan theta = 1 in n full turns
source: Theory P1-5.6 Quick check 3; 2n solutions of tan theta = 1 for 0 to 360 n degrees
stem: How many solutions of \(\tan\theta=1\) are there for \(0^\circ\le\theta\le {n|int}\times 360^\circ\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Tangent has period \(180^\circ\) and one solution of \(\tan\theta=1\) in each period. The given interval covers \({A|int}\) such periods, so there are \({A|int}\) solutions.
steps.note: One solution of tan theta = 1 in each 180 degrees.

contexts.note: Includes the original 360 degrees, two solutions

title: A quadratic trigonometric equation in a given interval

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

steps.name: s1
steps.text_tex: The identity \(\sin^2\theta=1-\cos^2\theta\) is used, to obtain \(8(1-\cos^2\theta)+6\cos\theta+1=0\), which rearranges to \(8\cos^2\theta-6\cos\theta-9=0\).
steps.note: Official MS: M1, expect 8 cos²θ − 6 cosθ − 9 = 0.

steps.name: s2
steps.text_tex: The quadratic is solved by factors, the formula, or completing the square, and the method is shown: \((4\cos\theta+3)(2\cos\theta-3)=0\).
steps.note: Official MS: A1, factors or formula or completing square must be shown.

steps.name: s3
steps.note: Official MS: AWRT, ignore solutions outside the given range; answer in radians scores A0.

title: A mixed sine-cosine equation, a sketch, and an inequality

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem:
(i) Solve the equation \(2\cos x+3\sin x=0\), for \(0^\circ\le x\le 360^\circ\). [3]

(ii) Sketch, on the same diagram, the graphs of \(y=2\cos x\) and \(y=-3\sin x\) for \(0^\circ\le x\le 360^\circ\). [3]

(iii) Use your answers to parts (i) and (ii) to find the set of values of \(x\) for \(0^\circ\le x\le 360^\circ\) for which \(2\cos x+3\sin x>0\). [2]

steps.name: s1
steps.note: Official MS: M1, use of tan = sin/cos to get tan =, or other valid method to find sin or cos =. M0 for tan x = +/- 3/2.

steps.name: s3
steps.note: Official MS: A1FT, 326.3 degrees awrt. FT for 180 added to an incorrect first answer in the given range. The second A1 is withheld if any further values in the range 0 to 360 are given. Answers in radians score A0, A0.

steps.name: s4
steps.text_tex: (ii) A sketch of \(y=2\cos x\): one complete cycle, starting and finishing at the top of the curve at roughly the same positive y-value and going below the x-axis by roughly the same distance.
steps.note: Official MS: B1, sketch of y = 2 cos x. One complete cycle; start and finish at top of curve at roughly the same positive y value and go below the x axis by roughly the same distance. (Can be a poor curve but not straight lines.)

steps.name: s5
steps.text_tex: (ii) A sketch of \(y=-3\sin x\): one complete cycle, starting and finishing on the x-axis, inverted, and going below and then above the x-axis by roughly the same distance.
steps.note: Official MS: B1, sketch of y = -3 sin x. One complete cycle; start and finish on the x axis, must be inverted and go below and then above the x axis by roughly the same distance. (Can be a poor curve but not straight lines.)

steps.name: s6
steps.text_tex: (ii) The two sketches are fully correct, with the sine curve of clearly larger amplitude than the cosine curve, and with reasonable curves.
steps.note: Official MS: B1, fully correct answer including the sine curve with clearly larger amplitude than cosine curve. Must now be reasonable curves. Note: separate diagrams can score 2/3.

steps.name: s7
steps.note: Official MS: B1FT, x < 146.3 degrees. Does not need to include 0 degrees, 360 degrees. Follow through from their answers in (i).

steps.name: s8
steps.note: Official MS: B1FT, x > 326.3 degrees. Allow a combined statement as long as the inequalities are correct if taken separately. SC: for two correct values including follow-through but with less-than-or-equal and greater-than-or-equal, B1.
